name: Tap drill size and drill-size decimal equivalents
description: Two related lookups machinists and hobbyists need together: (1) which tap drill to use for a given inch or metric thread (e.g. 1/4-20 UNC needs a #7 drill for approximately 75% thread engagement), and (2) the decimal-inch size of every number, letter, fraction and metric drill, so a shop can pick the nearest drill it actually owns. Two independent vendor sources are used for each table so a disagreement between them can be flagged rather than silently trusted. Answers 'what size do I drill before tapping 1/4-20', and 'what decimal is a #7 drill' — a complete range in one place beats looking up one size at a time.
licence: Factual compilation with source citations. Tap drill sizes and drill decimal equivalents are standard machining facts (ANSI/ASME B1.1 practice), not the vendor's original expression; short attributed quotes link back to the published table.
